title: DsNA(Digital sigNature for Audios): A Unique Method to Fingerprint Audio Files Generated by Text to Speech
abstract: The rapid advancement of text-to-speech (TTS) systems has enabled the large-scale generation of highly natural synthetic speech, raising critical concerns around audio provenance, authenticity, and misuse. In this work, we present DsNA (Digital sigNature for Audios), a lightweight post-generation fingerprinting framework designed to embed verifiable signatures directly into TTS-generated audio. Unlike traditional audio fingerprinting methods that rely on external matching or feature extraction, DsNA introduces a structured embedding mechanism in which a cryptographic signature derived from the audio and metadata is partitioned into shards and interleaved with segmented audio chunks. Preliminary evaluation demonstrates that the proposed method maintains audio fidelity, with no observable degradation in signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) between original and fingerprinted audio. This paper discusses this idea, that enables intrinsic identification of generated speech while preserving signal quality.
relevance_note: Post-generation fingerprinting of TTS audio for provenance; a TTS-agnostic watermark applied after synthesis, consistent with rejected post-hoc watermark precedents (MelShield, Latent-Mark).
